sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: In a combative opening day of the NATO summit in Brussels, President Trump went after Germany, calling it a captive of Russia and calling other member countries delinquent,
sentences.zh: 在布鲁塞尔北约峰会充满火药味的开幕日，特朗普总统抨击了德国，称其为俄罗斯的俘虏，并指责其他成员国拖欠会费，

sentences.en: where his frustration is coming from.
sentences.zh: 他的挫败感由此而来。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月12日，星期四。

sentences.en: Michael, the story of NATO really starts with three countries, the United States, the Soviet Union, and Nazi Germany.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，北约的故事实际上始于三个国家：美国、苏联和纳粹德国。

sentences.en: David Sanger is a national security correspondent for the Times.
sentences.zh: 大卫·桑格是《纽约时报》的国家安全记者。

sentences.en: Now, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当时，美国

sentences.en: and the Soviets, of course, were allies of convenience against Germany.
sentences.zh: 和苏联当然是为了对抗德国而结成的权宜盟友。

sentences.en: But it all came to a very ugly end as soon as victory in Europe was declared in April 1945.
sentences.zh: 但随着1945年4月欧洲胜利日的宣布，这种关系很快以非常糟糕的方式结束了。

sentences.en: And at that moment, the big concern moved away from a Nazi Germany that could threaten Europe to a Soviet Union that could do so.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，人们的主要担忧从可能威胁欧洲的纳粹德国，转向了可能造成同样威胁的苏联。

sentences.en: So right after the war was over, there was a great fear that vulnerable countries that had been initially taken over by the Nazis, from Poland, Denmark, Belgium,
sentences.zh: 因此，战争刚一结束，人们就非常担心那些最初被纳粹占领的脆弱国家，从波兰、丹麦到比利时，

sentences.en: could all fall under the influence of a communist Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 都可能落入共产主义苏联的势力范围。

sentences.en: So over time, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，美国

sentences.en: came around to the idea that the Soviet Union had to be contained.
sentences.zh: 开始意识到必须遏制苏联。

sentences.en: The gravity and the situation which confronts the world today necessitates my appearance before a joint session of the Congress.
sentences.zh: 当今世界所面临的严峻形势，迫使我必须出席国会联席会议。

sentences.en: And Harry Truman went to Congress in 1947 and laid that out.
sentences.zh: 哈里·杜鲁门在1947年来到国会，阐述了这一点。

sentences.en: I believe...
sentences.zh: 我相信……

sentences.en: He said that, I believe it must be the policy of the United States...
sentences.zh: 他说，我相信这必须成为美国的政策……

sentences.en: ...to support free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation by armed minorities or by outside pressures.
sentences.zh: ……去支持那些正在抵制武装少数派或外部压力试图征服的自由人民。

sentences.en: And that was really the beginning of the liberal international order.
sentences.zh: 那确实是自由国际秩序的开端。

sentences.en: The idea that the United States was going to be a guarantor of freedom around the world.
sentences.zh: 即美国将成为世界各地自由的保障者的理念。

sentences.en: So how did the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么美国是如何

sentences.en: actually put that into practice?
sentences.zh: 真正将其付诸实践的呢？

sentences.en: Well, almost as soon as Truman uttered those words, a series of crises came up.
sentences.zh: 嗯，几乎在杜鲁门说出这些话的同时，一系列危机就出现了。

sentences.en: The election, which lasts almost two full days, is held under the watchful eyes of 300,000...
sentences.zh: 这场持续了近两天的选举，是在30万人的注视下进行的……

sentences.en: The Soviets were meddling in the Italian elections in 1948.
sentences.zh: 1948年，苏联干预了意大利的选举。

sentences.en: The United States also meddled in those elections.
sentences.zh: 美国也干预了那场选举。

sentences.en: Both Western powers and Russia exerts strong pressure.
sentences.zh: 西方大国和俄罗斯都施加了强大的压力。

sentences.en: Czechoslovakia in 1948 is an established democracy...
sentences.zh: 1948年的捷克斯洛伐克是一个成熟的民主国家……

sentences.en: The Soviets overthrew a democratically elected government in Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 苏联推翻了捷克斯洛伐克民选的民主政府。

sentences.en: On February 25th, informed that the alternative is civil war, and aware of unmistakable threats of invasion from the Soviet Union if he does not capitulate,
sentences.zh: 2月25日，在被告知如果不投降就面临内战，并意识到如果拒绝投降将面临苏联明确的入侵威胁后，

sentences.en: President Behnisch accepts a communist cabinet.
sentences.zh: 贝内什总统接受了一个共产主义内阁。

sentences.en: And then, of course...
sentences.zh: 然后，当然……

sentences.en: June 1948.
Two and one-half million people cut off, isolated from the outside world.
sentences.zh: 250万人被切断联系，与世隔绝。

sentences.en: The Soviets cut off all access to West Berlin.
sentences.zh: 苏联切断了通往西柏林的所有通道。

sentences.en: Now, their food and fuel for their homes and factories could no longer be brought to them overland.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们的家庭和工厂所需的食物和燃料无法再通过陆路运送给他们。

sentences.en: And the United States ended up mounting what became called the Berlin Airlift.
sentences.zh: 于是美国最终发起了所谓的“柏林空运”。

sentences.en: The people in the western sector of Berlin have learned to live with the sight and sound of these giant four-engine aircraft.
sentences.zh: 西柏林的居民已经习惯了这些巨大的四引擎飞机发出的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: For the past year, this has been their only hope.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，这是他们唯一的希望。

sentences.en: Which flew in supplies to keep the people of West Berlin alive, and in many ways to keep this one little haven of democracy alive as well.
sentences.zh: 这些飞机运送物资以维持西柏林人民的生存，在许多方面也维持了这片民主小绿洲的生存。

sentences.en: And, David, how does the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，美国是如何

sentences.en: respond to this aggression from the Soviet Union?
sentences.zh: 应对苏联的这种侵略的呢？

sentences.en: Well, starting in 1948, the Truman administration realized that they were going to actually need to put together some kind of military alliance.
sentences.zh: 嗯，从1948年开始，杜鲁门政府意识到他们实际上需要建立某种军事联盟。

sentences.en: If there is anything certain today, if there is anything inevitable in the future, it is the will of the people of the world for freedom and for peace.
sentences.zh: 如果说今天有什么是确定的，如果说未来有什么是不可避免的，那就是世界人民对自由与和平的意志。

sentences.en: By April of 1949, Harry Truman had gathered together ministers from around Europe, and they stood in the State Department auditorium and signed this alliance.
sentences.zh: 到1949年4月，哈里·杜鲁门召集了欧洲各国的部长，他们在国务院礼堂签署了这个联盟。

sentences.en: We will now proceed to the signing of the North Atlantic Treaty.
sentences.zh: 我们现在开始签署《北大西洋公约》。

sentences.en: And that created NATO.
sentences.zh: 这就建立了北约。

sentences.en: The treaty shall enter into force between the states which have ratified it, including the ratifications of...
sentences.zh: 该条约将在已批准该条约的国家之间生效，包括……的批准书。

sentences.en: And where exactly is NATO?
sentences.zh: 那么北约到底是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it's basically just a military alliance to defend Europe against what was the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它基本上就是一个为了防御当时苏联而建立的军事联盟。

sentences.en: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed by Norway, Denmark, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, France, Italy, Portugal, the United Kingdom, Iceland, Canada, and the United States.
sentences.zh: 《北大西洋公约》由挪威、丹麦、荷兰、比利时、卢森堡、法国、意大利、葡萄牙、英国、冰岛、加拿大和美国签署。

sentences.en: But the key piece of NATO is something called Article 5 in its founding document.
sentences.zh: 但北约的核心是其创始文件中所谓的“第五条款”。

sentences.en: And that basically says...
sentences.zh: 它基本上是说……

sentences.en: They were sworn to stand together against aggression.
sentences.zh: 他们誓言要团结一致，共同抵御侵略。

sentences.en: An attack against one would be an attack against all.
sentences.zh: 对一个成员国的攻击就是对所有成员国的攻击。

sentences.en: An attack on one country is an attack on all.
sentences.zh: 对一国的攻击就是对全体的攻击。

sentences.en: And the idea was to create some sense of deterrence so that the Soviets knew that if they tried to pick off
sentences.zh: 其目的是建立一种威慑感，让苏联知道，如果他们试图挑衅

sentences.en: even the weakest member of NATO in Europe, they were going to be fighting everyone, including the United States.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是欧洲北约中最弱小的成员国，他们也将与所有人为敌，包括美国。

sentences.en: So, David, this is a military alliance based in Europe, created by the U.S., designed to rebuff a single enemy, the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，这是一个总部设在欧洲、由美国创建、旨在抵御单一敌人——苏联的军事联盟。

sentences.en: Yes, that was the goal.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是目标。

sentences.en: I say without hesitation that I am absolutely convinced that NATO provides the best, if not the only hope of peace.
sentences.zh: 我毫不犹豫地说，我绝对相信北约提供了和平的最佳希望，如果不是唯一的希望的话。

sentences.en: You know, Michael, there was this cheeky line early in NATO's history from General Hastings Ismay, who was the first secretary general of NATO.
sentences.zh: 你知道，迈克尔，北约历史上早期有一句俏皮话，出自北约第一任秘书长黑斯廷斯·伊斯梅将军之口。

sentences.en: He said the purpose of NATO was to keep the Soviet Union out, the Americans in, and the Germans down.
sentences.zh: 他说，北约的目的是“把苏联挡在外面，把美国留在里面，把德国压在下面”。

sentences.en: The leaders of the communist world meet in Warsaw to sign the treaty, which is their answer to NATO.
sentences.zh: 共产主义世界的领导人在华沙会面并签署条约，这是他们对北约的回应。

sentences.en: And the Soviets respond by creating their own sort of NATO.
sentences.zh: 苏联通过建立他们自己的“北约”来回应。

sentences.en: It was called the Warsaw Pact, and it had communist nations that were under Soviet influence,
sentences.zh: 它被称为华沙条约组织，成员包括受苏联影响的共产主义国家，

sentences.en: Poland, Bulgaria, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, of course, East Germany.
sentences.zh: 波兰、保加利亚、捷克斯洛伐克、匈牙利，当然还有东德。

sentences.en: And they were a military alliance of their own.
sentences.zh: 他们组成了自己的军事联盟。

sentences.en: So you saw these two groups of military allies facing off against each other.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到了这两组军事盟友在相互对峙。

sentences.en: The West must at all times maintain its own strength as long as the possibility of aggression exists.
sentences.zh: 只要侵略的可能性存在，西方就必须时刻保持自身的力量。

sentences.en: Only thus can we safeguard that peace for which the peoples of the world are longing.
sentences.zh: 只有这样，我们才能捍卫世界人民所渴望的和平。

sentences.en: And how does this new organization, NATO, operate day to day?
sentences.zh: 那么这个新组织——北约，日常是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: How is it funded?
sentences.zh: 它是如何获得资金的？

sentences.en: How does it function?
sentences.zh: 它是如何发挥作用的？

sentences.en: Well, there isn't a completely separate NATO military force of any kind.
sentences.zh: 嗯，并没有一个完全独立的北约军事力量。

sentences.en: They don't have their own army.
sentences.zh: 他们没有自己的军队。

sentences.en: Instead, they pooled together the military forces of each of the member countries.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们汇集了每个成员国的军事力量。

sentences.en: And over time, they learned how to train together and put their doctrine together.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们学会了如何共同训练并统一作战条令。

sentences.en: But the whole thought is that they just get organized under one European supreme commander appointed by the United States.
sentences.zh: 但核心思想是，他们都在由美国任命的一位欧洲最高指挥官的领导下进行组织。

sentences.en: And of course, it's the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当然，美国

sentences.en: that's always been at the core of NATO because it had the biggest forces.
sentences.zh: 一直是北约的核心，因为它拥有最强大的军事力量。

sentences.en: It had the most money and it had the most sophisticated intelligence.
sentences.zh: 它拥有最多的资金和最先进的情报。

sentences.en: And of course, Britain, the United States, and later France had nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 当然，英国、美国和后来的法国拥有核武器。

sentences.en: And the whole idea was that if you pool these together, you create a pretty fearsome deterrent.
sentences.zh: 整个想法是，如果你把这些力量汇集起来，你就能创造出一种相当可怕的威慑力。

sentences.en: And in fact, that's pretty well worked.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这确实非常有效。

sentences.en: What do you mean that it worked?
sentences.zh: 你说的“有效”是什么意思？

sentences.en: Think about all the wars that didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 想想所有没有发生的战争。

sentences.en: We never saw a nuclear war breakout in Europe, although it was threatened frequently.
sentences.zh: 我们从未看到核战争在欧洲爆发，尽管它经常受到威胁。

sentences.en: In the 50s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 在50年代和60年代。

sentences.en: And of course, the Soviets knew that the United States was keeping missiles in Turkey, nuclear weapons in Belgium.
sentences.zh: 当然，苏联知道美国在土耳其部署了导弹，在比利时部署了核武器。

sentences.en: That in other words, forces were forward deployed and under some NATO control or could be moved to NATO control fairly quickly.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，部队是前沿部署的，并处于某种北约控制之下，或者可以相当快地转移到北约控制之下。

sentences.en: And that made them think twice.
sentences.zh: 这让他们不得不三思而后行。

sentences.en: So the original idea of NATO,
sentences.zh: 所以北约最初的构想，

sentences.en: which is the symbolism of all of these countries kind of locking arms militarily and assuring each other that they will go to war to protect one another.
sentences.zh: 即所有这些国家在军事上携手合作，并向彼此保证将为保护对方而战的象征意义。

sentences.en: This has its desired goal of keeping the Soviet Union at bay.
sentences.zh: 这达到了将苏联拒之门外的预期目标。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It plain old worked.
sentences.zh: 它确实奏效了。

sentences.en: And it was, in retrospect, a pretty genius invention.
sentences.zh: 回顾过去，这是一个相当天才的发明。

sentences.en: It's probably Truman's greatest single legacy.
sentences.zh: 这可能是杜鲁门最伟大的遗产。

sentences.en: So NATO is working and the Soviet Union falls in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 所以北约在运作，而苏联在20世纪80年代解体了。

sentences.en: So it seems like that would be a highly logical time for NATO, which was created to protect Europe against the Soviet Union, to dissolve.
sentences.zh: 那么，对于一个为了保护欧洲免受苏联威胁而建立的北约来说，这似乎是一个解散的绝佳时机。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, that question came up very quickly after 1989.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个问题在1989年之后很快就出现了。

sentences.en: It really dominated debate in George H.W.
sentences.zh: 在苏联解体时，这确实主导了乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush's administration as the Soviet Union was breaking apart.
sentences.zh: 布什政府的辩论。

sentences.en: And the question was just a very basic one, which is, do we need NATO anymore?
sentences.zh: 问题非常简单：我们还需要北约吗？

sentences.en: We won.
sentences.zh: 我们赢了。

sentences.en: You know, we don't have this huge, hulking Soviet Union with the power to expand across Europe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不再面对那个拥有在欧洲扩张能力的庞大苏联了。

sentences.en: If anything, Russia, which inherited the Soviet Union's nuclear weapons and all of its problems, appeared to be shrinking.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么变化的话，那就是继承了苏联核武器及其所有问题的俄罗斯，似乎正在萎缩。

sentences.en: So the rationale for NATO was just falling apart.
sentences.zh: 所以北约存在的理由正在瓦解。

sentences.en: And there were a lot of people saying it should simply disband, that there was just no political reason anymore and no military reason to hold on to it.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多人说它应该直接解散，因为已经没有任何政治或军事理由继续维持它了。

sentences.en: But that's not what happened.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《纽约时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.zh: 当您首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，您在应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《纽约时报》应用程序，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: David, what happens to NATO after the Soviet Union falls?
sentences.zh: 大卫，苏联解体后北约发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, rather than disband, Michael, it actually expanded.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，它不仅没有解散，反而扩张了。

sentences.en: Many of the former Soviet republics who were suddenly finding themselves independent, Poland and Hungary, the Czech Republic, all the countries that made up,
sentences.zh: 许多突然发现自己独立的苏联前加盟共和国，波兰、匈牙利、捷克共和国，所有组成

sentences.en: or many of the countries that made up the old Warsaw Pact, were suddenly thinking to themselves they didn't want to be alone.
sentences.zh: 或者说许多组成旧华约的国家，突然想到他们不想孤军奋战。

sentences.en: They wanted to be part of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他们想成为西方的一部分。

sentences.en: And so they applied for membership in NATO.
sentences.zh: 于是他们申请加入北约。

sentences.en: And the big question was, should NATO let them in, even if that risked making Russia paranoid?
sentences.zh: 最大的问题是，即使这可能导致俄罗斯产生偏执，北约是否应该让他们加入？

sentences.en: And how does NATO and the U.S., its lead sponsor, respond to their desire to join?
sentences.zh: 那么北约及其主要赞助者美国，是如何回应他们加入的愿望的呢？

sentences.en: And there were debates about individual countries, and there were some debates that basically said,
sentences.zh: 关于个别国家存在辩论，也有一些辩论基本上说，

sentences.en: if the Russians came and knocked off this tiny little country like Estonia or Latvia or Lithuania, would we really go to war?
sentences.zh: 如果俄罗斯人来攻击像爱沙尼亚、拉脱维亚或立陶宛这样的小国，我们真的会开战吗？

sentences.en: Would we really invoke Article 5 to come to their defense?
sentences.zh: 我们真的会援引第五条款来保卫他们吗？

sentences.en: But in the end, people decided that the symbolism of having old members of the Warsaw Pact change teams and come over to NATO was worth it,
sentences.zh: 但最终，人们认为让旧华约成员国改换阵营加入北约的象征意义是值得的，

sentences.en: even if their military contribution was pretty tiny.
sentences.zh: 即使他们的军事贡献非常微小。

sentences.en: And what does Russia do in response to this expansion of NATO, a group that existed originally to rebuff the old Soviet Union?
sentences.zh: 那么俄罗斯对北约的这种扩张有何反应？这个组织最初可是为了抵御旧苏联而存在的。

sentences.en: Well, initially, not much until Vladimir Putin became president.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最初没什么反应，直到弗拉基米尔·普京成为总统。

sentences.en: And he viewed it as a humiliation.
sentences.zh: 他将其视为一种羞辱。

sentences.en: He viewed it as an effort to go steal from Russia, the core of the old Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他将其视为从俄罗斯——旧苏联的核心——窃取东西的企图。

sentences.en: And he was looking for an opportunity to get even.
sentences.zh: 他一直在寻找报复的机会。

sentences.en: Putin realized that Article 5 was something that would get invoked if he did a full military attack.
sentences.zh: 普京意识到，如果他发动全面军事进攻，就会触发第五条款。

sentences.en: But he didn't have the money or really the forces to sustain such an attack.
sentences.zh: 但他没有足够的资金，也没有真正的兵力来维持这样的进攻。

sentences.en: So he had to come up with a really targeted kind of disruption.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须想出一种真正有针对性的破坏方式。

sentences.en: Some way of harassing these countries, some way of undercutting their institutions,
sentences.zh: 某种骚扰这些国家的方法，某种削弱其体制的方法，

sentences.en: some way of making people no longer confident in their governments without actually bringing about an invocation of Article 5.
sentences.zh: 某种让人们不再信任其政府，却又不至于真正触发第五条款的方法。

sentences.en: First, he started rebuilding his nuclear forces, and then he started in with the cyber attacks, a very big one against Estonia.
sentences.zh: 首先，他开始重建核力量，然后开始发动网络攻击，其中针对爱沙尼亚的一次规模非常大。

sentences.en: Estonia faced a major crisis in 2007 when it became the first country to experience a massive cyber attack, which took down Estonia's email, bank and newspaper servers.
sentences.zh: 爱沙尼亚在2007年面临重大危机，当时它成为第一个遭受大规模网络攻击的国家，这次攻击导致爱沙尼亚的电子邮件、银行和报纸服务器瘫痪。

sentences.en: Another very big one against Georgia.
sentences.zh: 针对格鲁吉亚的另一次规模也非常大。

sentences.en: In 2008, paving the way for military action, Russia attacked Georgia's computer infrastructure, crippling the country.
sentences.zh: 2008年，为军事行动铺平道路，俄罗斯攻击了格鲁吉亚的计算机基础设施，使该国陷入瘫痪。

sentences.en: Two countries that, of course, had been all part of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 这两个国家当然都曾是苏联的一部分。

sentences.en: He did a series of attacks on Ukraine, not a NATO member,
sentences.zh: 他对乌克兰进行了一系列攻击，乌克兰不是北约成员国，

sentences.en: but he realized that the fact that they weren't a NATO member meant that NATO was not going to be tempted to come to their defense.
sentences.zh: 但他意识到，乌克兰不是北约成员国这一事实意味着北约不会有动力去保护他们。

sentences.en: And he used it as sort of his petri dish, the place where he could test out a number of ways of disrupting a society.
sentences.zh: 他把乌克兰当作自己的培养皿，一个可以测试多种破坏社会方式的地方。

sentences.en: The Russians are fully aware that Microsoft products, like all software, can be used as weapons in cyber warfare.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人完全清楚，微软产品像所有软件一样，可以在网络战中被用作武器。

sentences.en: He brought down the electric power grid in Ukraine twice.
sentences.zh: 他两次摧毁了乌克兰的电网。

sentences.en: And, of course, he meddled a bit in their elections as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，他也稍微干预了他们的选举。

sentences.en: Look at what Russia has done so far.
sentences.zh: 看看俄罗斯到目前为止所做的一切。

sentences.en: They're accused of having interfered or having tried to interfere in German, French, British and U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们被指控干预或试图干预德国、法国、英国和美国的

sentences.en: elections.
sentences.zh: 选举。

sentences.en: There's some evidence that he tried to meddle in the Brexit vote in Britain.
sentences.zh: 有一些证据表明他试图干预英国的脱欧投票。

sentences.en: He attempted and failed to meddle in the last French election.
sentences.zh: 他试图干预上一次法国大选，但失败了。

sentences.en: He's been trying this in Germany.
sentences.zh: 他一直在德国尝试这样做。

sentences.en: And, of course, Michael, he made his strongest effort to meddle in elections here in the United States in 2016.
sentences.zh: 当然，迈克尔，他在2016年对美国选举的干预力度最大。

sentences.en: Using many of the techniques that he had perfected against NATO and other Eastern European countries and former Soviet states.
sentences.zh: 使用了他针对北约、其他东欧国家和前苏联国家所完善的许多技术。

sentences.en: President Trump is slamming some of America's allies today during a high-stakes NATO summit in Brussels.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统今天在布鲁塞尔举行的高风险北约峰会上抨击了美国的一些盟友。

sentences.en: OK, so here we are now in 2018.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在是2018年了。

sentences.en: And leaders from the NATO countries have just gathered for a summit in Brussels.
sentences.zh: 北约国家的领导人刚刚聚集在布鲁塞尔参加峰会。

sentences.en: And President Trump is continuing to go after the military alliance.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统继续攻击这个军事联盟。

sentences.en: What exactly is President Trump's objection to it?
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统对它到底有什么不满？

sentences.en: Well, President Trump has had several objections to NATO over the years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多年来特朗普总统对北约有几点不满。

sentences.en: His first one is that it's really expensive.
sentences.zh: 他的第一个不满是它太贵了。

sentences.en: And many countries are not paying what they should.
sentences.zh: 而且许多国家没有支付他们应该支付的费用。

sentences.en: And, frankly, many countries owe us a tremendous amount of money from many years back where they're delinquent, as far as I'm concerned,
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，在我看来，许多国家拖欠了我们多年前欠下的巨额资金，

sentences.en: because the United States has had to pay for them.
sentences.zh: 因为美国不得不为他们买单。

sentences.en: And his second one is he doesn't believe that the United States gets very much out of these alliances.
sentences.zh: 他的第二个不满是他认为美国从这些联盟中得不到多少好处。

sentences.en: You know, we're protecting Germany, we're protecting France, we're protecting everybody, and yet we're paying a lot of money to protect.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在保护德国，保护法国，保护所有人，但我们却支付了大量的保护费用。

sentences.en: Now, this has been going on for decades.
sentences.zh: 这种情况已经持续了几十年。

sentences.en: He simply believes it costs a lot and that the benefits to us are hard to measure and probably negative.
sentences.zh: 他只是认为这花费巨大，而且对我们的好处难以衡量，甚至可能是负面的。

sentences.en: And is there any merit to his argument that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，他关于美国在北约问题上

sentences.en: is giving more than it gets when it comes to NATO?
sentences.zh: 付出多于回报的论点有道理吗？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, there's certainly some merit to the argument that the United States gives a lot to NATO and the European countries don't sacrifice as much in their own defense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，美国为北约付出了很多，而欧洲国家在自身防御上投入不足，这一论点当然是有一定道理的。

sentences.en: And that's not an argument that is new to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这并不是唐纳德·特朗普提出的新论点。

sentences.en: Our freedom isn't free, and we've got to be willing to pay for the assets, the personnel, the training that's required to make sure that we have a credible NATO force.
sentences.zh: 我们的自由不是免费的，我们必须愿意为确保拥有可靠的北约部队所需的资产、人员和训练买单。

sentences.en: Barack Obama used to make that argument, and that's why NATO countries got pressed to contribute more to their military forces during Obama's time.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马过去也提出过这个论点，这就是为什么在奥巴马时期，北约国家被施压要求为他们的军事力量做出更多贡献。

sentences.en: So there's nothing new, and there's certainly nothing wrong, in Donald Trump's fundamental complaint.
sentences.zh: 所以唐纳德·特朗普的基本抱怨并没有什么新鲜之处，当然也没有什么错。

sentences.en: What is different is that President Trump is the first American president to say, if this doesn't change on my terms, I may not come to your defense when that moment comes.
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，特朗普总统是第一位说“如果这不按我的条件改变，当那一刻到来时，我可能不会来保护你们”的美国总统。

sentences.en: I may ignore Article 5.
sentences.zh: 我可能会无视第五条款。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And Trump has actually said that.
sentences.zh: 而且特朗普确实说过那样的话。

sentences.en: President Trump said to me and Maggie Haberman during the presidential campaign, when I asked him,
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在总统竞选期间对我（和玛吉·哈伯曼）说，当我问他时，

sentences.en: would he come to the defense of a small former Soviet state like Estonia or something, if they were attacked by Russia,
sentences.zh: 如果像爱沙尼亚这样的小型前苏联国家受到俄罗斯攻击，他是否会去保护他们，

sentences.en: he said, the first thing I would do is check and see whether they fully paid up in what he calls NATO dues, but what the rest of the world knows is just their spending on defense.
sentences.zh: 他说，他要做的第一件事就是看看他们是否全额支付了他所谓的“北约会费”，但全世界都知道这只是他们的国防支出。

sentences.en: So he was essentially saying that if they call the fire department before the truck was sent out, someone was going to look up and see whether or not they'd paid their taxes.
sentences.zh: 所以他本质上是在说，如果他们拨打火警电话，在消防车出发之前，会有人去查一下他们是否缴纳了税款。

sentences.en: No one's ever heard an American president talk like that before, that in a time of emergency, he might think about not committing American defenses to help a NATO ally.
sentences.zh: 以前从未有人听过美国总统这样说话，即在紧急情况下，他可能会考虑不承诺动用美国防御力量来帮助北约盟友。

sentences.en: David, from everything you said, a lot of these original NATO countries and later NATO countries
sentences.zh: 大卫，从你所说的一切来看，很多这些最初的北约国家和后来的北约国家

sentences.en: rushed to the organization seeking defense from first the Soviet Union and now Russia and still live under the protective umbrella of NATO.
sentences.zh: 为了寻求保护，先是躲避苏联，现在是躲避俄罗斯，纷纷加入该组织，并且至今仍生活在北约的保护伞下。

sentences.en: So if they're not willing to pay the amount of money that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们不愿意支付美国期望他们支付的金额，

sentences.en: expects of them, isn't that a legitimate grievance on the part of President Trump, given that they still benefit from NATO?
sentences.zh: 考虑到他们仍然从北约受益，这难道不是特朗普总统的一个合理抱怨吗？

sentences.en: He certainly got a very legitimate point, as previous presidents have, that they need to go carry their own weight.
sentences.zh: 他当然有非常合理的观点，就像历任总统一样，他们需要承担起自己的责任。

sentences.en: Now, their response to this is, hey, we've not only carried our own weight, we've come in and invoked Article 5 to help you.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们对此的回应是：嘿，我们不仅承担了自己的责任，我们还曾援引第五条款来帮助你们。

sentences.en: In fact, the only time Article 5 was ever invoked in NATO's history was right after 9-11.
sentences.zh: 事实上，北约历史上唯一一次援引第五条款是在9·11事件之后。

sentences.en: And then NATO countries went in, some in large numbers and some in pretty small numbers, into both Iraq and Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 然后北约国家进入了伊拉克和阿富汗，有些投入了大量兵力，有些投入了相当少的兵力。

sentences.en: Now, their publics came to later on conclude that the United States had used the 9-11 attacks as a way to justify a truly unwise war in Iraq.
sentences.zh: 后来，他们的公众得出结论，认为美国利用9·11袭击作为借口，在伊拉克发动了一场极其不明智的战争。

sentences.en: And the politics of going into Iraq, that's been pretty poisonous to their future contributions to their defense budgets.
sentences.zh: 而进入伊拉克的政治后果，对他们未来在国防预算上的贡献产生了相当大的毒害作用。

sentences.en: And it has made them think twice about the wisdom of simply letting the United States drag them around as NATO decides what conflicts to enter and which ones not to.
sentences.zh: 这让他们在考虑是否仅仅因为北约决定进入哪些冲突、不进入哪些冲突而让美国牵着鼻子走时，不得不三思而后行。

sentences.en: As NATO leaders arrived for their two-day summit in Brussels, President Trump rocked the alliance with the accusation that Germany is, quote, totally controlled by Russia.
sentences.zh: 当北约领导人抵达布鲁塞尔参加为期两天的峰会时，特朗普总统指责德国“完全被俄罗斯控制”，这震撼了整个联盟。

sentences.en: Well, I have to say, I think it's very sad when Germany makes a massive oil and gas deal
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不得不说，我认为当德国与俄罗斯达成大规模石油和天然气交易时，这非常令人悲哀，

sentences.en: with Russia, where you're supposed to be guarding against Russia, and Germany goes out and pays billions and billions of dollars a year to Russia.
sentences.zh: 你们本应防范俄罗斯，而德国却每年向俄罗斯支付数十亿又数十亿的美元。

sentences.en: So we started by talking about these three countries, the U.S., Russia, and Germany, as being the three countries that explain the beginnings of NATO.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从谈论这三个国家——美国、俄罗斯和德国——开始，因为它们是解释北约起源的三个国家。

sentences.en: And I'm struck that the news out of the NATO summit today was that Trump was going after
sentences.zh: 令我震惊的是，今天北约峰会传出的消息是特朗普在攻击

sentences.en: Germany, saying that it was under the control of Russia.
sentences.zh: 德国，说它处于俄罗斯的控制之下。

sentences.en: But Germany is totally controlled by Russia, because they were getting from 60 to 70 percent of their energy from Russia and a new pipeline.
sentences.zh: 但德国完全被俄罗斯控制了，因为他们通过一条新管道从俄罗斯获得了60%到70%的能源。

sentences.en: David, what was that about?
sentences.zh: 大卫，那是怎么回事？

sentences.en: That seems like the ultimate insult to deliver at a NATO summit.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是在北约峰会上发出的终极侮辱。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was the ultimate insult.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是终极侮辱。

sentences.en: And it may have had more to do with his differences with Angela Merkel, the chancellor of Germany, than it did with any true belief.
sentences.zh: 这可能更多地与他与德国总理安格拉·默克尔的分歧有关，而不是出于任何真正的信念。

sentences.en: But the core of the argument was Germany gets an overwhelming amount of its natural gas, the fuel that keeps it warm in the winter, from Russia.
sentences.zh: 但论点的核心是，德国绝大部分的天然气——即冬天供暖的燃料——都来自俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And it's now building a new pipeline that will bring it in directly from Russia.
sentences.zh: 而且它现在正在建设一条直接从俄罗斯输送天然气的新管道。

sentences.en: And his basic argument is, how can you argue that you're standing up against Russia when you
sentences.zh: 他的基本论点是，当你资助俄罗斯时，你怎么能说你在对抗俄罗斯呢？

sentences.en: are funding Russia, because Russia is overly dependent on its energy exports, and when you're vulnerable to the Russians who can simply turn off the valve?
sentences.zh: 因为俄罗斯过度依赖其能源出口，而且当你面对可以随时关闭阀门的俄罗斯人时，你是脆弱的。

sentences.en: And what was the reaction from Germany?
sentences.zh: 那么德国的反应是什么？

sentences.en: It led many to question whether or not President Trump fundamentally believes in the NATO mission.
sentences.zh: 这导致许多人质疑特朗普总统是否从根本上相信北约的使命。

sentences.en: And that's a big question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: And I was at a conference of Europeans last weekend, where I had never before heard people
sentences.zh: 上周末我参加了一个欧洲人的会议，我以前从未听过人们

sentences.en: question whether or not they should go forward thinking that the United States would be the core of a future NATO.
sentences.zh: 质疑他们是否应该继续认为美国将成为未来北约的核心。

sentences.en: And for the first time, I heard them debating, could we continue with a NATO that didn't have the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次听到他们讨论，我们能否继续维持一个没有美国作为核心、

sentences.en: at the center, and one in which the United States wasn't the dominant voice in defense policy?
sentences.zh: 且美国不是国防政策主导声音的北约？

sentences.en: Putin and Trump are to meet in Helsinki, Finland, on July 16, just days after the president attends the NATO summit with America's closest allies.
sentences.zh: 普京和特朗普将于7月16日在芬兰赫尔辛基会面，就在总统与美国最亲密的盟友参加北约峰会几天后。

sentences.en: The president predicted that meeting Putin, quote, may be the easiest of all the sit-downs he has scheduled on his trip.
sentences.zh: 总统预测与普京的会面“可能是他行程中安排的所有会谈中最轻松的一次”。

sentences.en: David, I want to ask you about what's happening right after this NATO meeting ends, which seems particularly curious, given the history that you've just outlined for us.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我想问你关于这次北约会议结束后发生的事情，考虑到你刚才为我们概述的历史，这看起来特别令人好奇。

sentences.en: Right after this meeting ends in Brussels, President Trump is going to meet with Putin.
sentences.zh: 就在布鲁塞尔的这次会议结束后，特朗普总统将与普京会面。

sentences.en: What do you make of this timing?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待这个时机？

sentences.en: The problem isn't the meeting, Michael.
sentences.zh: 问题不在于会面本身，迈克尔。

sentences.en: The problem in their mind is Donald Trump's message.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，问题在于唐纳德·特朗普传达的信息。

sentences.en: If he was leaving NATO to stand up to Putin and say we're not going to tolerate the meddling in
sentences.zh: 如果他离开北约是为了对抗普京，并说我们不会容忍对选举的干预，

sentences.en: elections and we're not going to tolerate the continued occupation of Crimea and the harassment of
sentences.zh: 我们不会容忍对克里米亚的持续占领和对乌克兰的骚扰，

sentences.en: Ukraine, if that was his message, I think they'd be fine with the meeting happening right after NATO.
sentences.zh: 如果这是他传达的信息，我想他们会乐见这次会面在北约会议后立即举行。

sentences.en: Their problem is they don't actually believe that Donald Trump is going to stand up to Putin.
sentences.zh: 他们的问题是，他们并不真正相信唐纳德·特朗普会对抗普京。

sentences.en: And they're somewhat horrified at the imagery of him beating up publicly on television against his
